rules.sentence: Patients who survive an episode of ventricular fibrillation require a thorough history, physical examination, and targeted diagnostic workup to identify potential contributory and reversible causes.
Suspicion of IHD warrants evaluation with serum troponins, echocardiography, and, when indicated, emergent coronary angiography.

Echocardiography is typically performed to evaluate wall motion abnormalities associated with ongoing myocardial ischemia and to identify previously unrecognized valvular or structural heart disease that may have contributed to ventricular fibrillation.

Prompt or emergent coronary angiography should be considered due to the high prevalence of coronary events in this population.

Patients who have recovered from ventricular fibrillation may also require a cardiac electrophysiology study to differentiate inducible from noninducible ventricular fibrillation and to guide consideration for implantation of an internal cardiac defibrillator (ICD).
